briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. I will now begin the climate briefing for September 3, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Nepal's Great Flood and the Demand for Climate Justice
sections.content: Recently, Nepal has experienced record-breaking floods, resulting in immense loss of life and property damage, demanding urgent attention from the international community. Floods occurring along the Trishuli River in Nuwakot and Dhading districts between August 26 and September 1 have tragically increased the death toll from 1,135 to 1,243 as of September 2, with thousands more reported missing [34, 35, 36, 64]. The Prime Minister of Nepal directly linked this disaster to climate change, stating that Nepal is paying the price for the carbon emissions of developed nations. He presented a 'bill' demanding compensation for climate change damages from major emitters such as the United States, China, and India [1, 4, 48, 51, 62, 63]. This situation, coupled with the suffering of developing countries on the front lines of the climate crisis, once again strongly raises the issue of international responsibility for 'loss and damage'.

sections.title: ⚠️ UN Reports: Warning of Exceeding the 1.5°C Target
sections.content: Recent reports from the United Nations (UN) and the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) have warned that the international community's goal of limiting global warming to within 1.5°C is virtually unattainable and that this critical threshold will be exceeded within the next few years [45, 52, 53, 55, 56, 58, 61, 65]. While the reports clearly state that 'there are no good outcomes' if 1.5°C is surpassed, they also suggest that a path remains to reverse the global warming trend and return below the danger zone through aggressive climate action [52, 56, 65]. This once again reminds us that the climate crisis will not wait, emphasizing the need for fundamental transformation and robust responses to the complex crises humanity faces [2, 7].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Carbon Neutrality and Renewable Energy Transition Domestically and Internationally
sections.content: Domestically and internationally, efforts to expand renewable energy and implement various practices are continuing to achieve carbon neutrality goals. Hankook Tire plans to install a 5MW solar power facility at its Geumsan plant, aiming to produce 6.66 GWh of electricity annually and reduce carbon emissions by 3,061 tons. Hwaseong Special City has declared carbon neutrality implementation by quadrupling its renewable energy facility capacity [14, 15, 18, 22, 23, 25, 27, 29, 30, 31, 32, 33]. Furthermore, the Ministry of Climate has allocated 25.7319 trillion Korean Won for next year's budget, with approximately 10 trillion Won earmarked for power grid and renewable energy sectors [16, 28]. Various local governments and public enterprises, including Pohang City, Korea Western Power, Ansan Green Environment Center, and Chungcheongnam-do Province, are also actively pursuing this transition through carbon neutrality idea contests, waste resource exchange programs, and renewable energy investment agreements [8, 10, 12, 13, 20, 24, 26]. Internationally, a positive change was observed with China's second-quarter 2026 CO2 emissions decreasing by 1% due to a sharp drop in oil consumption [66, 70].

sections.title: ⚠️ Widespread Impacts of Climate Change and Policy Challenges
sections.content: Beyond the case of Nepal, climate change is impacting the world in various forms. Across the United States, autumn temperatures are rising [40]; wine producers are facing new challenges with earlier harvest seasons [42]; and in North American forests, ecosystems are rapidly changing, with black spruce forests being reshaped by pests and climate change [44]. The Executive Director of the European Environment Agency emphasized the severity of climate change, stating that it has already arrived and is causing suffering [46]. Meanwhile, in New York State, the 'Climate Change Superfund Act,' which sought to impose $75 billion on oil companies to cover climate change costs, was dismissed by a judge, highlighting policy challenges [37, 43, 49]. These examples demonstrate that climate change is not merely an environmental issue but a complex crisis affecting the economy and society as a whole [7].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing once again reminds us of the severity of the climate crisis and the urgent need for multifaceted efforts by the international community to overcome it. This concludes the climate briefing for September 3, 2026.
